epic.title: Home dashboard: the wall on the kitchen frame, then panels and controls
epic.description:
The kitchen photo frame shows the existing `/wall`, proved for a week before anything new is built; then a plain tile grid with one panel library and a set per room, house controls through Home Assistant (lights, plugs and scenes open, cameras and heating behind the PIN), and panels in the order they would be used: shopping and meals, baby log, cooking mode first; energy, parcels and music later. Speech only when asked, night hours per room, guest mode by tap and schedule, touches counted per tile from day one. Nothing is bought before Phil sees a costed list.

## Order
wall.01 identifies the frame; wall.02 runs the existing wall on it for a week (with MYC-205's PIN and pairing); wall.03 makes it boot into the wall and wake by touch; wall.04 refreshes the costed list and surveys owned devices at any time. wall.05 builds the tile library on the Field shell's tile grid. Then the panels by use: wall.06 (shopping and meals), wall.07 (baby log), wall.08 (cooking mode), wall.09 and wall.10 (chores, bins and fridge notes), wall.13, wall.14, wall.16; later wall.11 (parcels, after MYC-201), wall.12 (energy), wall.15 (music). Settings and behaviour: wall.19 (night hours), wall.20 (guest schedule), wall.23 (sound). Once Home Assistant and local names exist (sub.08, sub.05): wall.17 controls, then wall.18 doorbell, wall.21 idle status, wall.22 offline. wall.24 moves screens to the Smart-devices network after net.09; wall.25 adds rooms; wall.26 is the done check after wall.06.

## Done means
Both Phil and Kirsty use the kitchen screen daily for two weeks (wall.26).

## Flags
No [claude] flags touch this epic. One open design question is carried in wall.17: where the Home Assistant token lives.

## Dossier
The dossier is attached in Docs (link added by the integrator).

tickets.title: Identify the frame from the device itself: model, OS, browser version, full-screen ability
tickets.description:
## What
Find out what the A3 touch photo frame in the kitchen is, from the frame itself: brand and model from the label, the Android version and any photo app from its About screen, whether it has a browser or an app store, the browser's version, and so whether it can show `/wall` full-screen. One sitting of about 15 minutes, guided by the checklist. Nothing is reset, rooted or installed.

## Why
The wall's first screen is the frame Phil owns, and its purchase could not be found in his email (H10), so the answer starts from the device.

## Done looks like
The checklist's fields hold brand, model, Android version, browser and version, and a route (A, A2 or E); MYC-182's photo frame line carries the same answer.

## Unlocks
- wall.02: the week on the real frame (or the stand-in)
- wall.03: boot and full-screen, for this frame
- wall.04: the costed list knows whether a screen is needed

## Depends on
Nothing. Relates to MYC-182 (the frame answer lives there too).

steps_definition.title: Identify the kitchen photo frame from the device itself

intro.answer: Read the frame's label and its About screen, and find out whether it has a browser, so the wall knows which route it takes.
unlocks: wall.02: the existing wall on the real frame for a week
wall.03: boot straight into the dashboard
to_hand: Your phone, to photograph the label

hard_part.why: Many frames run one locked app (often Frameo) with no browser; that is an answer, not a problem, and nothing is forced open.

steps.title: Photograph the label

where.label: The back of the frame and its stand

steps.body_html: Look on the back, under the stand and on any sticker for a brand, a model code and an FCC ID. Photograph them and type them below.
steps.expect_html: You have a photo of a label with a brand, a model code, or an FCC ID.

steps.title: Open the About screen

where.label: The frame's own Settings

steps.body_html: On the frame open Settings. If it is a plain Android screen, go to About tablet (or About device). If it is a photo app such as Frameo, its own Settings > About. Note the Android version, the model shown there, and the app's name.
steps.expect_html: You can see an Android version, or the name of the photo app and its version.

notes.html: Do not choose Reset, Factory reset or anything that offers to erase. The photos on the frame would go.

steps.title: Look for a browser or an app store

where.label: The photo frame, in the kitchen

steps.body_html: Go to the frame's home screen or app list (swipe up, or the grid icon). Look for Chrome, a Browser app, or Play Store.
steps.expect_html: You know whether the frame has a browser, the Play Store, or neither.

steps.title: Read the browser's version

where.label: The frame's browser

steps.body_html: Only if 1.3 found a browser: open it and go to the address below. Write down the browser and version it shows. If there is no browser, skip this step.
steps.expect_html: The page names the browser and its version (for example Chrome 131 on Android 11).

steps.title: Full-screen check and the route

where.label: Your decision

steps.body_html:
Pick the line that fits:

  • A: a browser or the Play Store is there. The wall runs on the frame; wall.03 installs a kiosk browser.
  • A2: only a locked photo app (Frameo or similar). Stop here; the frame stays a photo frame for now and wall.04's costed list decides the screen.
  • E: not sure. Use a phone or tablet you already own for wall.02's week.

Then type the same answer into MYC-182.
steps.expect_html: One route is chosen and written below, and MYC-182's photo frame line is answered with brand, model and route.

notes.html: Opening a locked frame needs its maker's beta programme, a cable and often rooting. That can leave the frame unusable. It is not part of this guide; if you want it, it becomes its own ticket.

steps_definition.finish_html: The frame has a name and a route. wall.02 puts the existing wall on it (or on the stand-in) for a week.

tickets.title: The existing wall on the real frame, lived with for a week; nothing new built until it works
tickets.description:
## What
Pair the frame (or the stand-in device wall.01 chose) as the Kitchen wall, using MYC-205's PIN and Settings > Security > Walls, then live with the existing `/wall` for seven days: one glance a day noted in the checklist, and a five-minute talk with Kirsty on day 7. If the Field shell lane's tile board is live by then, it is what the frame shows; `?board=classic` keeps the old board.

## Why
Phil decided the first thing proved is the existing wall on the real frame, lived with for a week; nothing new is built until that works (answer 15).

## Done looks like
Seven daily notes and a day-7 answer (keep, missing, frame good enough) in the checklist; the Kitchen wall listed in Settings > Security > Walls.

## Unlocks
- wall.05: the tile library starts from the week's notes

## Depends on
- wall.01: which device and route
- MYC-205: the PIN and the Kitchen wall (same steps, done first)

## Red team
- Finding 53: The week is lived with the classic board (the one proved so far); wall.05 moves the tile grid onto the frame after it.

tickets.title: Boot straight into the dashboard, full-screen, touch wake: a ticket per device type (the frame first)
tickets.description:
## What
On the kitchen frame (route A from wall.01): install Fully Kiosk Browser from the Play Store or the vendor's APK, set its start address to `/wall`, turn on launch on boot, full-screen and kiosk mode with an exit PIN, switch the lock screen off, and make a touch the only wake: Android's screen timeout set to the longest and Fully's screensaver (black) doing the dimming, because many frames cannot be woken by touch once Android switches the screen off. Then the plug test. This ticket is the frame; each further device type gets its own copy of the guide, written by Claude when wall.25 picks the device (Fire tablets differ: Fully cannot always switch their screens back on).

## Why
Phil decided screens boot straight into the dashboard, full-screen, with a ticket per device type, and wake by touch only (answers 17 and 18).

## Done looks like
After a power cut the frame shows the wall full-screen without a tap, goes dark after ten quiet minutes, and one touch brings it back; the checklist records whether PLUS was needed.

## Unlocks
- wall.25: the guide copied for each further device type
- wall.19: per-room night hours act on a screen that stays on

## Depends on
- wall.01: the route must be A (a browser or the Play Store); on A2 or E this ticket waits for wall.04's choice
- wall.02 helps (the wall already paired) but is not required

## Cost
Fully Kiosk PLUS is about 8.90 EUR plus tax per device, one-off (vendor licence page, checked 2026-11-28). Only if a feature Phil needs shows the watermark. Nothing is bought in this run.

steps_definition.title: Boot the kitchen frame straight into the wall, full-screen, woken by touch

intro.answer: Install Fully Kiosk Browser on the frame, point it at the wall, start it on boot, and use its screensaver so a touch wakes it.
unlocks: wall.25: the same guide copied per further device
wall.19: night hours per room act on a screen that stays on
to_hand: The wall already paired on the frame (wall.02)
A 6 to 8 digit exit PIN for the kiosk, your choice
time: about 15 minutes for wake and the power test

hard_part.why: If Android switches the screen fully off, many frames cannot be woken by touch; the screensaver does the dimming instead.

sources.label: Fully Kiosk not launching at boot

phases.title: Install and point at the wall

steps.title: Route check

where.label: Your decision

steps.body_html: Open wall.01's checklist and read the route field.
steps.expect_html: wall.01's route is A. If it is A2 or E, stop: this guide is for a frame that has a browser or the Play Store.

steps.title: Install Fully Kiosk Browser

where.label: The frame's Play Store, or the vendor site in its browser

steps.body_html: In the Play Store search Fully Kiosk Browser and install it. With no Play Store, download the APK from the vendor site in the frame's browser and allow the install when asked.
steps.expect_html: Fully Kiosk Browser opens on the frame.

troubleshooting.symptom: The frame refuses apps from outside a store
troubleshooting.fix: Stop and note it on the ticket; do not change security settings to force it.

steps.title: Set the start address

where.label: Fully Kiosk > Settings > Web Content Settings

steps.body_html: Set Start URL to the Mycelium address followed by /wall. Back out; if the wall asks for a code, make one in Settings > Security > Walls (Re-pair) and type it.

blocks.label: Path to add to the Mycelium address

steps.expect_html: Fully shows the wall; the pairing from wall.02 may need a fresh code.

steps.title: Start on boot, full-screen, kiosk mode

where.label: Fully Kiosk > Settings

steps.body_html: Turn on Launch on Boot, Fullscreen Mode (under Web Browsing or Device Management, by version), then Enable Kiosk Mode with your exit PIN. Accept when Android asks to make Fully the home app.
steps.expect_html: The status bar and navigation are hidden and Fully asks to become the home app.

notes.html: Keep the exit PIN in Proton Pass under the frame's name. Do not write it in this checklist.
Some features show a watermark until the PLUS licence is bought (about 8.90 EUR per device). Nothing is bought in this run; note which ones.

steps.title: Lock screen off

where.label: The frame's own Settings

steps.body_html: In the frame's Android Settings > Security (or Lock screen), set screen lock to None.
steps.expect_html: Restarting the frame does not show a swipe-to-unlock screen.

phases.title: Touch wake and the power test

steps.title: Android screen timeout to the longest

where.label: The frame's own Settings

steps.body_html: Settings > Display > Screen timeout: the longest choice.
steps.expect_html: Display > Screen timeout shows the longest value, or Never.

steps.title: Screensaver instead of screen off

where.label: Fully Kiosk > Settings > Screensaver

steps.body_html: Set Screensaver Timer to 600 seconds and Screensaver Brightness to 0; leave the screensaver address empty (black). Do not use the screen-off timer. The wall's own ambient plate still runs before the screensaver.
steps.expect_html: After the set time the screen goes dark, and one touch brings the wall back.

troubleshooting.symptom: A touch does not wake it
troubleshooting.fix: Turn off any Screen Off Timer in Fully and in Android power saving; the screensaver must be the only thing dimming.

steps.title: Pull the plug

where.label: The photo frame, in the kitchen

steps.body_html: Unplug the frame for ten seconds and plug it back in. Do not touch it.
steps.expect_html: Within about two minutes of power returning the frame shows the wall, full-screen, with no tap.

steps.title: Note what is left

where.label: Your decision

steps.body_html: Write the three results and whether any feature showed the PLUS watermark. Claude copies this guide for each further device type when wall.25 picks one.
steps.expect_html: The ticket says whether the frame boots, fills the screen and wakes by touch, and whether PLUS is needed.

steps_definition.finish_html: The frame starts in the wall on its own and wakes to a touch. A device of another type gets its own copy of this guide.

tickets.title: Costed hardware list refreshed (docs/run/wall-report.md) and the devices he already owns surveyed; nothing bought before he sees it
tickets.description:
## What
Claude refreshes the costed table in `docs/run/wall-report.md` ("If the frame cannot run a browser") with today's UK prices and adds the lines the dossier found: A2 (a locked Frameo-type frame, not opened), C2 (a 21.5 inch touch monitor with a Pi 5), the Fully PLUS price (about 8.90 EUR per device), the Pi 5 rises of 2026 (8 GB bare board about £168), and a Glow display for live energy data if wall.12 goes that way. Then a survey of what Phil already owns that could be a screen for the living room, bedroom and office: old phones, tablets, laptops, Fire or Echo Show devices, TVs and sticks (net.09's device list and the home inventory are the starting point), each with whether it has touch, a current browser and a kiosk route. The result is a table Phil reads; the dossier's section 3.7 is the first draft.

## Why
Phil decided nothing is bought until he has seen a costed list, and extra screens are devices he already owns, researched first (answers 8 and 26).

## Done looks like
The report's table carries today's date, every price has a source and a checked date, and a second table lists owned devices with a yes or no for touch, browser and kiosk route. Nothing ordered.

## Unlocks
- wall.25: further rooms pick from the owned-devices table
- wall.03: a non-frame device's guide starts from its row

## Depends on
Nothing. Reads wall.01's answer if it exists (route A2 or E makes the table the next decision).

## Cost
Prices only; nothing is bought in this run or by this ticket.

tickets.title: Tile library and per-device sets: same panels, a different set per room; touches per tile counted from day one
tickets.description:
## What
Build the wall's panel library on the Field shell's tile grid: the lane building that grid tonight (Stream U, lane U2) draws `WallGlance` as `TilesBoard`, a 6-column grid with what is on today largest (4 by 2), people 2 by 1, weather and bins 1 by 1, the baby line 2 by 1 and a greeting by time of day. This ticket turns those tiles into a library: each panel registered once with its sizes, each wall device (`wall_devices`) holding its own ordered set chosen in Settings > Security > Walls, so the kitchen, living room, bedroom and office draw different sets from the same panels. Every tile tap is counted per device and tile from the first day (a small table in the family space, no titles or content stored), and Settings shows a count per tile for the last 30 days so unused tiles can be dropped. The finance guard test and `e2e/wall.phil.spec.ts` keep passing; no money field enters the contract.

## Why
Phil decided the wall is its own plain tile grid, the same panel library with a different set per device, and that touches per tile are counted from day one so unused tiles are dropped (answers 20 and 21, 6b).

## Done looks like
Two walls paired to the family show different tile sets chosen in Settings; a tap on a tile raises its count in Settings; the classic board still opens at `?board=classic`; build, unit tests and the wall e2e spec pass.

## Unlocks
- wall.06 to wall.16, wall.19, wall.20, wall.23: every panel and setting plugs into the library
- wall.25: further rooms are a set each

## Depends on
- wall.02: the week on the real frame (nothing new before it works)
- The Field shell's tile grid (lane U2, this run): the base this builds on

## Red team
- Finding 53: Moves the tile grid onto the frame after wall.02's week; adds a short greeting by time of day (6b).

tickets.title: Panel: shopping list and meal plan
tickets.description:
## What
A tile pair for the kitchen: this week's meal plan (tonight's meal large, as 6b's 7am kitchen asks) and the shopping list, with tick-off and add by touch. The data lives today in the health section (`shopping_lists`, `meal_plan`), which is personal space the wall cannot read. First step: Claude proposes a family-space shopping list and meal plan (shared by Phil and Kirsty) and asks on the ticket before moving or copying any of Phil's own rows; until he answers, the tile shows only what the family space holds.

## Why
Phil decided shopping and meals come first by use, and the shopping list pad is one of the four paper things the wall replaces (answers 11 and 16, 6b).

## Done looks like
On the kitchen wall, tonight's meal shows large, an item can be ticked off and added by touch, and the same list is on both phones; nothing from Phil's personal space appears without his answer on the ticket.

## Unlocks
- wall.26: the done check leans on this panel being used daily
- wall.08: cooking mode opens from tonight's meal

## Depends on
- wall.05: the tile library this panel registers in

tickets.title: Panel: baby log
tickets.description:

Move the built baby line (the last log line and the feed, nappy and sleep taps on today's board, `lib/family/babylog.ts`) into the tile library as its own panel, add the time since the last feed and sleep, and an undo for a mistaken tap within a minute. Family space only, as now.

## Why
Phil decided the baby log is one of the first panels by use (answers 12 and 16).

## Done looks like
The baby tile shows the last line and time since the last feed and sleep, the three taps log as today, and a wrong tap can be undone for a minute.

- wall.26: daily use in the kitchen
- BABY epic: the log on the wall once the baby is here

## Depends on

tickets.title: Panel: cooking mode
tickets.description:
## What
A full-screen cooking view opened from tonight's meal or a recipe: large steps one at a time, swipe or tap to move on, timers by touch with a soft chime, the screen kept awake, and the ambient and night dimming held off while it is open. Recipes are personal space today (`recipes`, `gousto_recipes`); the ticket starts by asking which recipes the kitchen may show (family copies, or behind the PIN).

## Why
Phil decided cooking mode is among the first panels by use (answers 12 and 16).

## Done looks like
A recipe opens full-screen on the kitchen wall, steps move by touch, two timers can run with a chime, and the screen does not dim while cooking.

## Unlocks
- wall.26: daily use in the kitchen

## Depends on
- wall.05: the tile library this panel registers in
- wall.06 helps (tonight's meal opens it)

tickets.title: Panel: chores rota (new)

A new chores rota in the family space: chores with who and how often, shown on the wall as today's and this week's jobs per person, ticked off by touch with the chime. PW-22 (the house cleaning schedule) is the content source; the rota is built so its schedule can be entered once and reused.

tickets.title: Panel: energy use (smart meter, EV charger)
tickets.description:
## What
A tile with today's and this week's electricity (and gas, if the meter gives it) in kWh, and the EV charger's last session. Never pounds: the finance guard forbids money on the wall. First step, written up on the ticket before any build: the meter route. n3rgy's consumer access now needs a business partner's consent and is not dependable; Hildebrand's Bright app and its cloud API give half-hourly data free; live local data needs a Glow display and MQTT enabled by Hildebrand (a purchase). The EV charger's make decides its route (its cloud API or a Home Assistant integration). If the Home Assistant route is chosen, this waits for sub.08.

## Why
Phil decided energy use is a panel, from the smart meter and the home EV charger (answers 11 and 13).

## Done looks like
The route is written on the ticket and agreed; the tile shows today's kWh and the last charge; no pound figure appears anywhere on the wall.

## Unlocks
Nothing further.

## Depends on
- wall.05: the tile library this panel registers in
- sub.08: Home Assistant, only if the Home Assistant route is chosen

## Cost
A Glow display is a purchase, to be priced in wall.04 if the live route is wanted. Nothing is bought in this run.

tickets.title: Panel: photo slideshow from a shared phone album (a new connection)
tickets.description:
## What
A slideshow tile, and the ambient and guest views' pictures, from one shared phone album. First step, a choice for Phil on the ticket: (a) an iCloud Shared Album with Public Website on, read through an undocumented Apple endpoint (anyone with the link can see the photos; adding photos needs an Apple device); (b) Immich on the Substrate box (private, needs Substrate); Google Photos is out because its API cannot read shared albums since 31 March 2025. Then the connection, cached thumbnails served through Mycelium so the screen does not fetch from Apple directly (wall.24), and a pause by touch.

## Why
Phil decided the slideshow comes from a shared phone album, a new connection, not the Family timeline (answer 22).

## Done looks like
The route is chosen on the ticket; a photo added to the album appears on the wall within a day; the frame never loads images from outside Mycelium.

## Unlocks
- wall.16: "from the archive" can draw photos from the same album

## Depends on
- wall.05: the tile library this panel registers in

tickets.title: Panel: music, Spotify control on whichever speaker is playing
tickets.description:
## What
A tile showing what is playing and where, with play, pause, skip and volume, and a list of speakers to move playback to. First step: check the existing Spotify app (`lib/spotify/client.ts`) against the February 2026 Development Mode rules (the owner needs Premium, five authorised users per app, a narrower endpoint set; whether playback control is in it is unverified) and add the control scopes. Speakers appear only while a Spotify client is active on them and some models refuse Web API commands, so the tile controls the active speaker reliably and shows "start it from the app" when an idle one will not wake. The wall uses a household token held on the server, never in the page.

## Why
Phil decided music is Spotify control on whichever speaker is playing (answer 23).

## Done looks like
With music playing anywhere in the house, the wall shows it and pause, skip and volume work; a speaker that cannot be reached shows a plain line, not an error.

## Unlocks
Nothing further.

## Depends on
- wall.05: the tile library this panel registers in

tickets.title: Panel: "from the archive", quotes and photos from this day in past years
tickets.description:
## What
A small tile rotating saved quotes (`lib/quotes`) and photos taken on this day in past years. Quotes are Phil's space today; the tile shows only quotes he marks for the family, and photos only from the shared album (wall.14) or the family space.

## Why
Phil asked for a small "from the archive" tile rotating saved quotes and photos from this day in past years (6b).

## Done looks like
On a day with a marked quote or an old photo, the tile shows it; with none, the tile hides.

## Unlocks
Nothing further.

## Depends on
- wall.05: the tile library this panel registers in
- wall.14 helps (photos)

tickets.title: House controls through Home Assistant: lights and plugs, scenes open; cameras and heating behind the PIN
tickets.description:
## What
Control tiles on the wall for lights, plugs and scenes, open to anyone at the screen, and for cameras and heating, opened only after a person's quick-unlock PIN. All through Home Assistant on the Substrate box (REST `POST /api/services/<domain>/<service>`, WebSocket for live state). The wall page comes from Vercel over HTTPS, so calling Home Assistant from the screen needs Home Assistant on a local HTTPS name with a real certificate (sub.05) and the Mycelium origin in its `cors_allowed_origins`. The cautious design, written up for Phil before the build: a dedicated non-admin Home Assistant user for the walls with only lights, plugs and scenes; camera and heating calls made by the Mycelium server after the PIN. Lighting positions from home.24 appear as scene buttons.

## Why
Phil decided all four controls, through Home Assistant, with lights and scenes open and cameras and heating behind the quick-unlock PIN (answers 9, 10, 29).

## Done looks like
From the kitchen wall a light and a scene work with no PIN; heating and a camera ask for a PIN first; the wall's Home Assistant user cannot change heating on its own (checked by a call that is refused).

## Unlocks
- wall.18: the doorbell pop-up
- wall.21: house status when idle
- wall.22: controls that keep working with the internet down
- glass epic: voice house control comes after this

## Depends on
- wall.05: the tile library
- sub.08: Home Assistant on the Substrate box
- sub.05: local HTTPS names with real certificates (added by this rundown; see the dossier section 5)

## Flag
Where the Home Assistant token lives (each screen, or the server only) is a security choice; the ticket proposes the narrow wall user and waits for Phil's answer before the build.

tickets.title: Doorbell pop-up on a shared-room screen, cameras on demand
tickets.description:
## What
When the doorbell rings, shared-room walls (kitchen, living room; not the bedroom) show the doorbell camera full-screen for about 30 seconds with a soft chime, then go back. Other cameras open on demand behind the PIN, as wall.17 set. The ring arrives from Home Assistant's event stream; the picture is the local camera stream through Home Assistant, never a cloud link.

## Why
Phil decided cameras on a shared-room screen pop up when the doorbell rings and are otherwise on demand (answer 14).

## Done looks like
A ring shows the doorbell on the kitchen wall within a couple of seconds and it returns to the board by itself; the bedroom screen does not pop up.

## Unlocks
Nothing further.

## Depends on
- wall.17: house controls and the PIN rule for cameras

tickets.title: Night hours per room in Settings; bedroom wind-down (dim, tomorrow's first thing, dark)
tickets.description:
## What
Night hours exist today as one fixed window, 23:00 to 06:00 London, for every wall (`lib/wall/schedule.ts`). Move them into Settings > Security > Walls per device. Add the bedroom wind-down: at a set time the screen dims, shows tomorrow's first thing (the first family appointment, or the first item of whoever unlocks it), then goes dark until morning or a touch.

## Why
Phil decided night hours are fixed per room and set in Settings, and the bedroom screen winds down: dims, shows tomorrow's first thing, then dark (answer 19, 6b).

## Done looks like
Two walls with different night hours dim at their own times; the bedroom wall dims, shows tomorrow's first thing and then goes dark; a touch wakes it.

## Unlocks
Nothing further.

## Depends on
- wall.05: the tile library this panel registers in

Guest mode exists as one tap (clock, weather, pictures, long press to leave). Add a schedule Phil sets in Settings (for example a weekend when people stay) and the choice of which walls it applies to, one or all; a scheduled guest mode also starts and ends by itself.

## Why
Phil decided guest mode is one tap by hand and on a schedule he sets, choosing which device or all (6b).

## Done looks like
A schedule set in Settings puts the chosen walls into guest mode at its start and back at its end; the one tap still works on any wall.

## Unlocks
Nothing further.

tickets.title: Idle: house status (doors, heating, what is on)
tickets.description:
## What
When the wall is idle, the ambient view gains a quiet house status line from Home Assistant: doors open or shut, the heating's current and set temperature, and which lights or plugs are on. Read-only on the idle view; control stays on the tiles.

## Why
Phil decided the idle screen shows house status: doors, heating, what is on (6b).

## Done looks like
With the wall idle, opening a door or switching a light changes the status within a few seconds.

## Unlocks
Nothing further.

- wall.17: the Home Assistant connection

tickets.title: Offline: last known board with an "as of" time; controls keep working locally
tickets.description:
## What
With the internet down, the wall keeps the last board it drew (the app's offline store, `lib/offline`) with an "as of" time, and lights, plugs and scenes still work by calling Home Assistant on its local HTTPS name directly. The page must be served from the cache when Vercel cannot be reached, and the ticket checks that the wall device's sign-in survives a few hours offline. Proved by pulling the router's internet line, not by a simulation alone.

## Why
Phil decided that with the internet down the board shows its last state with an "as of" time, and controls keep working locally (answer 28).

## Done looks like
With the internet line unplugged, the kitchen wall shows the board with an "as of" time and a light still switches from it.

## Unlocks
Nothing further.

## Depends on
- wall.17: house controls
- sub.05: local HTTPS names (direct local calls need them)

## Red team
- Finding 58: Includes the PC-off test: everything works except controls and the PC voice (6.25).

## What
Today the wall speaks nudges, the morning pick and family reminders aloud on its own every twenty seconds (`thingsToSay`, `lib/wall/speak.ts`). Change that: nothing is said unless someone asks ("Read my morning", or a tap on a speak button on a tile); reminders and nudges become a soft natural chime and a line on the screen. Replace the chime with a small set of soft natural sounds and a volume per device in Settings.

## Why
Phil decided soft natural chimes, and speech only when asked for, which narrows the earlier spoken reminders decision for the wall (6b).

## Done looks like
A nudge arriving on the wall makes a soft chime and a line, and says nothing; "Read my morning" still speaks; each wall has its own volume.

## Unlocks
Nothing further.

## Depends on
- wall.05: the tile library this panel registers in

tickets.title: Screens on the Smart-devices network, reaching Mycelium and Home Assistant only
tickets.description:
## What
Move each wall screen onto the Smart-devices network and limit what it may reach to Mycelium and Home Assistant. Claude first writes on the ticket the names a wall needs (the Mycelium address, Home Assistant's local name, the kiosk app's licence check, and any image host the panels use unless Mycelium serves them). Phil then does one sitting per screen with the checklist. Mycelium is on Vercel's shared and changing addresses, so the limit is by name in the DNS filter (sub.06), not by address on the router; until the filter exists the screen gets the Smart-devices network's rules and the allow step waits.

## Why
Phil decided screens sit on the Smart-devices network, allowed to reach Mycelium and Home Assistant only (answer 27).

## Done looks like
Each screen is on Smart devices, the wall loads, and once sub.06 exists a general site does not open from the screen.

## Unlocks
- wall.22: the screen on the same network as Home Assistant

## Depends on
- net.09: the smart devices moved to Smart devices
- sub.06: the DNS filter, for the allow step (added by this rundown; see the dossier section 5)

steps_definition.title: Put the wall screens on the Smart-devices network, reaching Mycelium and Home Assistant only

hard_part.why: Mycelium is on Vercel's shared and changing addresses, so the router cannot allow it by address; the allow list has to be by name, in the DNS filter.

steps.title: Join the Smart-devices Wi-Fi

where.label: The frame's own Settings

steps.expect_html: The screen shows it is connected to the Smart-devices network.

steps.title: The wall still loads

where.label: The photo frame, in the kitchen

where.label: Router admin, the client list

steps.expect_html: The screen is listed on the Smart-devices network with a name you recognise.

steps.title: Apply the allow list

where.label: The DNS filter (sub.06), the screen's group

steps.body_html: Put the screen in a group allowed only the names Claude listed on the ticket. If the DNS filter does not exist yet, stop here: the screen stays on Smart devices with that network's rules, and this step waits for sub.06.
steps.expect_html: The screen is in a group that allows only the listed names; the wall still loads afterwards.

troubleshooting.symptom: The wall goes blank after the allow list
troubleshooting.fix: Move the screen out of the group to bring it back, then add the name the browser's error page shows to the ticket.
